question_stem: A nucleus of bismuth-212 (²¹²₈₃Bi) decays by the emission of an α-particle and γ-radiation.
question_stem_latex: A nucleus of bismuth-212 (${}^{212}_{83}\mathrm{Bi}$) decays by the emission of an $\alpha$-particle and $\gamma$-radiation.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text: State the number of protons and the number of neutrons in the nucleus of bismuth-212.
parts.question_text_latex: State the number of protons and the number of neutrons in the nucleus of bismuth-212.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
The γ-radiation emitted from the nucleus has a wavelength of 3.8 pm.
Calculate the frequency of this radiation.
parts.question_text_latex:
The $\gamma$-radiation emitted from the nucleus has a wavelength of $3.8\,\mathrm{pm}$.
Calculate the frequency of this radiation.

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
Explain how a single beam of α-particles and γ-radiation may be separated into a beam of
α-particles and a beam of γ-radiation.
parts.question_text_latex: Explain how a single beam of $\alpha$-particles and $\gamma$-radiation may be separated into a beam of $\alpha$-particles and a beam of $\gamma$-radiation.

parts.label: (d)
parts.question_text:
The α-particle emitted from the bismuth nucleus has an initial kinetic energy of 9.3 × 10⁻¹³ J.
As the α-particle moves through air it causes the removal of electrons from atoms. The α-particle loses energy and is stopped after removing 1.8 × 10⁵ electrons as it moves through the air.
Determine the energy, in eV, needed to remove one electron.
parts.question_text_latex:
The $\alpha$-particle emitted from the bismuth nucleus has an initial kinetic energy of $9.3 \times 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{J}$.
As the $\alpha$-particle moves through air it causes the removal of electrons from atoms. The $\alpha$-particle loses energy and is stopped after removing $1.8 \times 10^{5}$ electrons as it moves through the air.
Determine the energy, in eV, needed to remove one electron.
